Kindness Resilience Respect Community
Welcome to Millbrook Park CE Primary School
Where every child flourishes, every day.
Welcome to Millbrook Park CE Primary School and Nursery, a vibrant, ambitious and inclusive Church of England school where children are inspired to love learning, discover their talents and become confident, compassionate citizens of the future.
Nestled within London's beautiful Green Belt, our exceptional learning environment provides children with endless opportunities to learn, explore and grow. Our modern facilities, extensive outdoor grounds, woodland learning area and 3G sports pitch ensure that learning extends far beyond the classroom, encouraging curiosity, creativity and adventure every day.
At Millbrook Park, we believe every child is unique. Guided by our Christian vision and values, we nurture each child's academic, social, emotional and spiritual development so that they leave us not only with excellent knowledge and skills, but with the confidence, kindness and resilience to make a positive difference in the world.
We are proud to offer an ambitious, knowledge rich curriculum that inspires children to think deeply, ask questions and develop a lifelong love of learning. Through exceptional teaching, high expectations and carefully planned enrichment opportunities, every child is encouraged to achieve their very best. Whether performing on stage, representing the school in sport, exploring our woodland, programming robots, conducting scientific investigations or discovering the wider world through educational visits, every experience is designed to broaden horizons and build confidence.
Our school is much more than a place of learning. It is a community where children feel safe, valued and genuinely known. Warm relationships, exceptional pastoral care and a culture of kindness ensure that every child belongs and every family is welcomed as part of the Millbrook Park community.
We know that children achieve their greatest success when schools and families work together. We value the strong partnerships we build with parents and carers and believe that open communication, mutual trust and shared aspirations enable every child to flourish.
As you explore our website, we hope you gain a sense of the warmth, ambition and excitement that make Millbrook Park such a special place. Here you will find information about our curriculum, Christian vision, school life and the many opportunities that make every day memorable for our children.
If you are considering Millbrook Park for your child, we would be delighted to welcome you for a visit. Seeing our school in action is the best way to experience the joyful atmosphere, purposeful learning and caring relationships that define our community.
We look forward to welcoming you and your family to Millbrook Park CE Primary School, where children flourish, dreams grow and futures begin.

Art and Design
At Millbrook Park, we believe every child is an artist. Our art curriculum helps pupils develop creativity by first building strong artistic knowledge and skills. Children learn to draw, paint, sculpt and create with increasing confidence while exploring the work of significant artists, designers and craft makers from different cultures and time periods.
Our curriculum follows the National Curriculum and is carefully sequenced using the Kapow Primary scheme. Skills are revisited and developed year after year so that children build mastery over time. Pupils learn the formal elements of art, such as line, shape, colour, tone, texture and pattern, before applying these techniques in increasingly creative and independent ways.
Children work in sketchbooks throughout each unit to explore ideas, practise techniques and reflect on their learning. They study the work of artists, discuss how and why artworks were created, and learn to evaluate both their own work and that of others using appropriate artistic vocabulary. We believe that learning to talk about art is just as important as learning to create it.
By the end of Year 6, pupils have developed the confidence to express themselves creatively, the technical skills to produce high-quality artwork, and the knowledge to appreciate and discuss art from a wide range of cultures, traditions and historical periods. Through art, children develop resilience, curiosity, imagination and pride in their own unique creative journey.

PHONICS AT MILLBROOK
Phonics
At Millbrook Park Primary School, early reading is taught using synthetic phonics as the main approach to reading. We follow the phonics scheme 'Read Write Inc'.
Pupils are systematically taught to identify phonemes (sounds), how to blend the sounds to make words for reading, first orally and then in print and how to segment the sounds in order to write words. They are taught to use their phonic skills and knowledge as their first approach to reading, but are also taught high frequency words which do not follow the phonic rules and need to be learnt by sight.

YEAR 1 PHONICS SCREENING CHECK
At the end of Year 1, children will undertake a statutory phonics screening check.
This is a short assessment to make sure that children have learnt phonics to an appropriate standard.
There are 40 words in the screening check which children are asked to read on a one-to-one basis with their teacher. The check is made up of 'real words' (eg. 'mud') and 'non-words' (eg. 'splog') and children need to apply their phonic knowledge to read all words.
Preparation for the check takes place during the daily phonics session, but you can help your child at home by practising phonics on a regular basis.

WRITING AT MILLBROOK
Writing Curriculum
Our writing curriculum develops confident, fluent and ambitious writers through a carefully sequenced, research-informed approach. We believe that children write best when they have first mastered the foundations of writing, so our curriculum prioritises sentence construction, grammar, vocabulary, spelling, punctuation and handwriting before moving towards extended composition.
From the Early Years onwards, children develop their writing through rich talk, storytelling and oral rehearsal. We use carefully selected texts to immerse pupils in high-quality texts, enabling them to learn, imitate and innovate language before writing independently. Oracy is at the heart of every lesson, helping children organise their ideas and build confidence as communicators.
Across the school, pupils practise writing every day through explicit teaching, modelled examples, daily dictation, handwriting and purposeful grammar instruction. These routines develop automaticity in the core skills, allowing children to focus on expressing their ideas creatively and effectively.
Vocabulary is taught explicitly through carefully chosen texts, while grammar is always taught in context so that children understand how language creates meaning. High-quality model texts (WAGOLLs) and structured teacher modelling support pupils as they move from guided practice to independent writing.
By the end of Year 6, pupils write with accuracy, stamina and creativity across a wide range of genres. They have a secure understanding of grammar and language, can adapt their writing for different audiences and purposes, and leave as articulate, confident writers who are well prepared for the next stage of their education.
The Importance of Dictation
At Millbrook Park CE Primary School, dictation is a daily part of our English curriculum because it strengthens the essential foundations of successful writing. Rather than simply testing spelling, dictation brings together spelling, punctuation, grammar and handwriting in one purposeful activity, helping children apply their knowledge automatically and accurately.
Research shows that when transcription skills become automatic, children have more mental capacity to think about the content, organisation and creativity of their writing. By reducing the cognitive effort required to remember spellings or punctuation, dictation frees working memory so pupils can focus on communicating their ideas effectively.

History
History Curriculum
Our History curriculum inspires children to become curious, knowledgeable historians who understand how the past has shaped the world we live in today. Through a carefully sequenced curriculum, pupils develop a secure understanding of British and world history, building knowledge chronologically from their own lives and local history in the early years to ancient civilisations, medieval Britain and the modern world by the end of Key Stage 2.
Chronology is at the heart of our curriculum, helping children understand when events happened and how societies, ideas and cultures have changed over time. Alongside historical knowledge, pupils learn to think like historians by asking questions, analysing evidence, considering different viewpoints and explaining why events were significant.Throughout the curriculum, children revisit key first-order concepts that help them make meaningful connections across time. They explore power, from ancient rulers and monarchies to democracy, social justice and modern government; religion, examining how beliefs have shaped communities, conflict and culture; civilisation, discovering how societies have developed through settlement, trade, technology and innovation; and communication, tracing the journey from the earliest forms of writing to modern media, understanding both its power to inform and its influence on society. These themes are woven through each year group, enabling pupils to see the links between different periods of history and the world around them.
Children also develop increasingly sophisticated historical thinking through the concepts of change and continuity, cause and consequence, significance, and similarity and difference. Rich stories, artefacts, historical enquiry, visits and ambitious vocabulary bring history to life while helping pupils develop confidence in discussing and explaining the past.
By the end of Year 6, pupils have a secure chronological understanding of British and world history, can interpret evidence thoughtfully, appreciate the diversity of past societies, and understand how history continues to influence our lives today. They leave Millbrook Park as informed, reflective and inquisitive historians who are ready to make sense of the future by understanding the past.

Maths
All of our pupils are taught for maths mastery using concrete, pictorial and abstract methods.
Mathematics mastery is a journey that children will acquire throughout their primary school life and beyond.
It is about giving children the best chance of developing a deep, long-term and flexible understanding of the subject. At any one point of a child’s journey through our school, achieving mastery means having a solid enough understanding of the mathematics that has been taught to enable him/her to move on to more advanced material.
VISION
Our shared vision is for children to develop an appreciation for mathematics and see it as a subject where they can explore and be creative.
They should be curious and enjoy their mathematical learning; understanding that it will play a significant role in their future. At the end of each year, children should master their age-related expectations and have a firm foundation upon which to build.
AIMS
The national curriculum for mathematics aims to ensure that all pupils:
In order to support children’s development in maths, we have introduced a variety of exciting resources to help motivate, support and challenge pupils in mathematical concepts.
Through our mastery approach to maths our aim is to give children the tools and strategies to move from using concrete resources to being confident at using abstract approaches in their learning. Too many parents share the example where the they have only been taught abstract strategies and without concrete understanding there can be weaknesses in the understanding. We want our children to be confident mathematicians who can prove their strategies are correct and use reasoning across the curriculum.
PROBLEM SOLVING AND REASONING
Problem solving and reasoning are two vital skills in mathematics that promote deep mathematical understanding.
These skills can sometimes overlap and may be used hand in hand. For example when starting to solve a problem, reasoning skills may be needed if there are a range of possible starting points. Fundamentally, they are two separate skills and teachers should understand what they are and how they are different.

TIMES TABLES
We expect all children at Millbrook Park to have a secure grasp of the multiplication tables.
Just like learning to walk before you can run, learning multiplication and memorising the times tables are building blocks for other maths topics taught in school - higher learning such as division, long multiplication, fractions and algebra. Students who do not memorise the times tables will find these levels of maths much more difficult than they need to be. Students who have not mastered their tables will very often fall behind in maths (and other subjects that use maths) and begin to lose confidence. We ask parents for support in helping their children to learn the multiplication tables.
